narrative_summary: The S&P 500 broke out to new highs at 7,600.50, clearing the entire 23.6-61.8% fib band and the 7/22 swing high in a five-session vertical thrust that lifted extension to +8.13% above the 200-day and pinned price on the upper Bollinger Band. The technical skeleton is now fully restored — 50-day above a rising 200-day, VIX at 15.86 below its 50-day MA, junk spreads tightening to 1.28 — but the internals refuse to confirm: McClellan breadth sits at its cycle-low shelf (874.59), net new highs slipped to 1.04, and 5-day MFI spiked into the trim zone near 91 while ERP stays pinned at 0.31% in the valuation-ceiling band. Monte Carlo has flipped back to 56.23% up-first, yet that still fails the 70% Late Bull threshold for an eighth straight session, so no bullish action is authorized. This is a trim-into-strength tape: harvest into the 7,600-7,696 zone, add nothing, and wait for either breadth to expand or a mean-reversion test of the 7,468-7,504 band before considering re-entry.

Bollinger Bands are expanding upward with price walking the upper band on the 5-day and 1-month charts — strong-trend behavior, though extended (chart 02, 03).

Junk bond spread tightened to 1.28 (score 70), near the low end of the trailing range and below its 12-month average line — credit is confirming risk appetite (chart 15).
Rally Exhaustion Score is Low and realized 20-day vol is only 13.3%, so the simulation runs with full drift and tighter ranges rather than crisis assumptions.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Price has broken to new all-time highs with expanding Bollinger Bands and a rising 20/50-day cluster; breadth indicators are lagging, coincident measures that often catch up after an index breakout, and credit is simultaneously tightening, which argues the underlying risk appetite is real.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: McClellan Volume Summation sits at 874.59, a cycle-low shelf far beneath its February peak of ~1,370, and net new 52-week highs have slid to 1.04 from 1.18 even as the index prints records. Falling participation into new highs is the framework's explicit topping warning and signals extremely narrow leadership.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: When breadth and credit both diverge from price, elevate caution even if price has not yet broken down; falling sentiment/participation near new highs is a topping warning.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Overbought momentum in a confirmed uptrend is a strength signal: MFI above 80 and RSI above 70 during a breakout typically resolve by consolidation rather than reversal, and the 3-year chart shows repeated episodes of RSI running above 70 for weeks during bull legs.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: 5-day MFI spiked to ~91 and has already rolled to ~79 while price kept rising, and the 1-month RSI has pushed above the 70 trim line — both are trim-zone readings. conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: Trim zone: RSI above 70, MFI above 80. Bearish divergence: price makes a higher high while MFI or RSI makes a lower high; longer timeframe divergences carry more weight.

conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: The 7/29 decline never produced a 25-30 VIX capitulation spike, so the 7,316 low was never validated as a washout; the market has instead rallied 3.9% into a complacent sub-16 VIX at record price with cycle-low breadth. conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: A correction that unfolds without a volatility spike should be treated as orderly rather than capitulative; VIX below 15 is complacent, and moving-average support is less reliable when risk conditions shift abruptly.

primary_tension: A fully restored and now record-setting technical skeleton (new all-time high at 7,600.50, upper-band walk, 50-day above a rising 200-day, VIX 15.86, junk spread tightening to 1.28, Monte Carlo back to 56.23% up-first, Low exhaustion) is colliding with the most severe internal non-confirmation of the entire arc: McClellan breadth stuck at its 874.59 cycle-low shelf and net new highs falling to 1.04 as price makes new highs, 5-day MFI spiking to ~91 in the trim zone with RSI above 70, ERP pinned at 0.31% inside the valuation-ceiling band on a 4.686% 10-year, extension stretched to +8.13% above the 200-day, and the Monte Carlo edge still failing the 70% Late Bull threshold for an eighth consecutive session.
